newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banker sees 27.5 baht/dlr optimal in 3/6 mths.
newsitem.headline: Thai banker sees 27.5 baht/dlr optimal in 3/6 mths.

text.p: The president of the Thai Bankers Association said on Friday he thought the optimal rate for the baht in three to six months was 27.5 per dollar.
Olarn Chaipravat, who is chief executive of Siam Commercial Bank, also said he thought the current two-tiered foreign exchange system would stay permanently.

"The optimal average rate of the baht in three to six months that will produce the least impact for the economy (after the baht float) is 27.5 to the dollar provided that the government also adopted appropriate measures to allow Thai industries to improve their competitiveness," Olarn told a seminar.
Thai authorities on Wednesday announced they had changed to a managed float of the baht from the 13-year old system of pegging the currency to a basket of currencies.
The float caused the baht to drop nearly 20 percent in one day. The baht is currently trading around 28.60/29.10 to the dollar offshore and 28.50/29.00 in domestic markets.

The Bank of Thailand has said it would review the two-tier market after the baht stabilised both onshore and offshore. But Olarn said the two-tiered system, born after a May attack on the currency, was likely to stay.
"I believe the two-tier system will stay permanently because there is no point of lifting it after we learned that it helps in separating the two markets the same way they do in Singapore," he said.
